page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv6 family, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This low memory-to-core ratio positions the instance as a compute-focused option. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include any bundled local storage, requiring external premium storage attachments for disk operations. This lack of local storage, combined with the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, represents a key architectural tradeoff, making the instance less suitable for memory-intensive databases or massive local caching workloads.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ls_v6 demonstrates strong performance in several areas. It achieves strong ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as in single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is also strong at 205.24 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the instance delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 347.06 tokens per second for small LLM models and strong prompt processing speeds of 172.96 tokens per second for medium models. These characteristics make the instance suitable for compute-bound workloads, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference.
